arxiv-2008-00895.title: On second-order and fourth-order elliptic systems consisting of bulk and surface PDEs: Well-posedness, regularity theory and eigenvalue problems
arxiv-2008-00895.creator: Patrik Knopf, Chun Liu
arxiv-2008-00895.description: Abstract In this paper, we study second-order and fourth-order elliptic problems which include not only a Poisson equation in the bulk but also an inhomogeneous Laplace–Beltrami equation on the boundary of the domain. The bulk and the surface PDE are coupled by a boundary condition that is either of Dirichlet or Robin type.

arxiv-2012-06290.title: Double-peaked Lines, Dual VLBI Components, and Precessing Jets in J1328+2751
arxiv-2012-06290.creator: S. Nandi, A. Caproni, P. Kharb, B. Sebastian, R. Roy
arxiv-2012-06290.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by S. Nandi, A. Caproni, P. Kharb, B. Sebastian, R. Roy. In this work, we report a radio galaxy with precessing jets, double-peaked emission lines and the presence of two compact radio components with a projected separation of ∼ \sim 6 parsec in Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations. The emission line peak separations could be suggesting the presence of a supermassive black hole binary (BBH) with a separation of 6.3 parsec, matching the VLBI results.

arxiv-2201-01868.title: Bayesian inference and Markov chain Monte Carlo based estimation of a geoscience model parameter Journal: Computers and Geosciences
arxiv-2201-01868.creator: Saumik Dana, Karthik Reddy Lyathakula
arxiv-2201-01868.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Saumik Dana, Karthik Reddy Lyathakula. The critical slip distance in rate and state model for fault friction in the study of potential earthquakes can vary wildly from micrometers to few meters depending on the length scale of the critically stressed fault. This makes it incredibly important to construct an inversion framework that provides good estimates of the critical slip distance purely based on the observed acceleration at the seismogram. The framework is based on Bayesian inference and Markov chain Monte Carlo.

arxiv-2201-10233.title: A description of the minimal elements of Shi regions in classical Weyl Groups
arxiv-2201-10233.creator: Balthazar Charles \addressmark 1
arxiv-2201-10233.description: Abstract In this extended abstract, we show how a bijection between parking functions and regions of the Shi arrangement from [Athanasiadis, Linusson ’99] (in type A n A_{n} ) and [Armstrong, Reiner, Rhoades ’15] (in type B n , C n , D n B_{n},C_{n},D_{n} ) allows for the computation of the minimal elements of the Shi regions.

arxiv-2305-19323.title: Turbulent convection as a significant hidden provider of magnetic helicity in solar eruptions
arxiv-2305-19323.creator: Shin Toriumi, Hideyuki Hotta, Kanya Kusano
arxiv-2305-19323.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shin Toriumi, Hideyuki Hotta, Kanya Kusano. Solar flares and coronal mass ejections, the primary space weather disturbances affecting the entire heliosphere and near-Earth environment, mainly emanate from sunspot regions harbouring high degrees of magnetic twist. However, it is not clear how magnetic helicity, the quantity for measuring the magnetic twist, is supplied to the upper solar atmosphere via the emergence of magnetic flux from the turbulent convection zone. Here, we report state-of-the-art numerical simulations of magnetic flux emergence from the deep convection zone.

arxiv-2403-18817.title: Signatures of electronic ordering in transport in graphene flat bands
arxiv-2403-18817.creator: Archisman Panigrahi, Leonid Levitov
arxiv-2403-18817.description: Abstract Recently, a wide family of electronic orders was unveiled in graphene flat bands, such as spin- and valley-polarized phases as well as nematic momentum-polarized phases, stabilized by exchange interactions via a generalized Stoner mechanism. Momentum polarization involves orbital degrees of freedom and is therefore expected to impact resistivity in a way which is uniquely sensitive to the ordering type.

arxiv-2412-14033.title: Hansel: Output Length Controlling Framework for Large Language Models
arxiv-2412-14033.creator: Seoha Song, Junhyun Lee, Hyeonmok Ko
arxiv-2412-14033.description: Abstract Despite the great success of large language models (LLMs), efficiently controlling the length of the output sequence still remains a challenge. In this paper, we propose Hansel, an efficient framework for length control in LLMs without affecting its generation ability. Hansel utilizes periodically outputted hidden special tokens to keep track of the remaining target length of the output sequence.

arxiv-2506-08328.title: Supplementary Materials for “Diffusion Non-Additive Emulator for Multi-Fidelity Simulations with Tunable Precision”
arxiv-2506-08328.creator: Junoh Heo, Romain Boutelet and Chih-Li Sung
arxiv-2506-08328.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Junoh Heo, Romain Boutelet and Chih-Li Sung. Computer simulations are indispensable for analyzing complex systems, yet high‑fidelity models often incur prohibitive computational costs. Multi‑fidelity frameworks address this challenge by combining inexpensive low‑fidelity simulations with costly high‑fidelity simulations to improve both accuracy and efficiency. However, certain scientific problems demand even more accurate results than the highest‑fidelity simulations available, particularly when a tuning parameter controlling simulation accuracy is available, but the exact solution corresponding to a zero-valued parameter remains out of reach.

arxiv-2509-08121.title: An Algorithmic Upper Bound for Permanents via a Permanental Schur Inequality
arxiv-2509-08121.creator: Aditi Laddha, Madhusudhan Reddy Pittu
arxiv-2509-08121.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Aditi Laddha, Madhusudhan Reddy Pittu. Computing the permanent of a non-negative matrix is a computationally challenging, #P-complete problem with wide-ranging applications. We introduce a novel permanental analogue of Schur’s determinant formula, leveraging a newly defined permanental inverse . Building on this, we introduce an iterative, deterministic procedure called the permanent process , analogous to Gaussian elimination, which yields constructive and algorithmically computable upper bounds on the permanent.

arxiv-2509-20633.title: Affine Hulls and Simplices: a Constructive Analysis
arxiv-2509-20633.creator: Douglas S. Bridges
arxiv-2509-20633.description: Abstract This paper deals with certain fundamental results about affine hulls and simplices in a real normed linear space. The framework of the paper is Bishop’s constructive mathematics, which, with its characteristic interpretation of existence as constructibility , often involves more subtle estimation than its classical-logic-based counterpart.

arxiv-2510-18724.title: Adapting Language Balance in Code-Switching Speech
arxiv-2510-18724.creator: Enes Yavuz Ugan, Ngoc-Quan Pham, Alexander Waibel
arxiv-2510-18724.description: Abstract Despite achieving impressive results on standard benchmarks, large foundational models still struggle against code-switching test cases. When data scarcity cannot be used as the usual justification for poor performance, the reason may lie in the infrequent occurrence of code-switched moments, where the embedding of the second language appears subtly.

arxiv-2602-10454.title: LATA: A Tool for LLM-Assisted Translation Annotation Corresponding author: amaasiri@uqu.edu.sa
arxiv-2602-10454.description: Abstract The construction of high-quality parallel corpora for translation research has increasingly evolved from simple sentence alignment to complex, multi-layered annotation tasks. This methodological shift presents significant challenges for structurally divergent language pairs, such as Arabic–English, where standard automated tools frequently fail to capture deep linguistic shifts or semantic nuances.

arxiv-2602-18520.title: Sketch2Feedback: A Grammar-in-the-Loop Framework for Rubric-Aligned Feedback on Student STEM Diagrams
arxiv-2602-18520.creator: Aayam Bansal
arxiv-2602-18520.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Aayam Bansal. Providing timely, rubric-aligned feedback on student-drawn diagrams is a persistent challenge in STEM education. While large multimodal models (LMMs) can jointly parse images and generate explanations, their tendency to hallucinate undermines trust in classroom deployments. We present Sketch2Feedback , a grammar-in-the-loop framework that decomposes the problem into four stages—hybrid perception, symbolic graph construction, constraint checking, and constrained VLM feedback—so that the language model verbalizes only violations verified by an upstream rule engine.

pmc-12634669.title: Estimation of forest above-ground biomass based on stacked ensemble model in Chongqing, China
pmc-12634669.creator: Jinlian Liu, Zhiyun Chen, Bangxiang Luo, Ao Sun, Xuezhong Wen, Tongyi Huang
pmc-12634669.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Accurate regional-scale estimation of forest aboveground biomass (AGB) is critical for effective forest management and terrestrial carbon cycle research. However, applications integrating multiple machine learning models (MLs) for forest AGB estimation in mountainous forests remain limited. pmc-13474082.title: Decoding cytarabine-induced damage in the prepubertal testis: A multi-omics atlas of ecosystem and inheritance
pmc-13474082.creator: Siyu Xia, Jiangpeng Wu, Jiawei Duan, Wenting Ye, Yan Sun, Xiaojian Yang, Xiao Chen, Hongru Lin, Songyu Huang, Jing Cai, Haiping Wen, Yali Song
pmc-13474082.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryPediatric leukemia therapies can compromise future fertility, particularly in prepubertal boys who cannot bank sperm. We used dose-response histology, endocrine and sperm analyses, bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, and metabolomics to map cytarabine (Ara-C) injury in prepubertal mouse testes. Ara-C caused seminiferous-tubule disruption, hormone suppression, sperm loss, spermatogonial depletion linked to ferroptosis and replication arrest, stress remodeling of Sertoli and Leydig cells, and altered intercellular signaling centered on Sertoli hubs.
